ruling: - **R12.** Owner 16:10 CST Nov 10: "yes this statement of opus 4h etc also feels super arbitrary". And: "i dont want to do such rigid word grants moreso like if i say send a swarm of opus agents that just works too yanno? A is good though but it should be override <anytime> or override not just override and override 4h". One route reads the owner's own typed words for overrides and Opus asks alike, judged and fail closed. Agent or pasted text never grants, except a relay in R18 point 5's form (owner 09:10 CST Nov 11, below). Fast path, no model call: `override` (one act) or `override` with any length (15, 15m, 90 minutes, 2 hours, 4h). Any other wording is judged. Every grant prints one receipt line the owner sees (what it lifts, one act or until when); today a grant prints nothing. A refusal no override can lift says so. Departs from: decision owner-override, where a longer phrase such as "override 15m please" grants nothing; under R12 the judge reads it. Home: decision owner-override, rewritten in place. An override may travel by relay. Owner 09:10 CST Nov 11, in the coordinator's chat, to the question "may an override travel by relay?": "q1 -- yes". A relay counts only in R18 point 5's form: his exact words, their time, and the one session and act they cover, checked against the sender's feedback log. The receiving session prints the same receipt line. Until R18 point 5's check is built (stage 4), only his typed words and a page save grant an override. This changes decision owner-override's sentence "An override covers only the session where the owner typed it": a relay in that form reaches the one session it names.
